Subject: Private VPC: Tenant isolation & egress model clarification

Hi Maya / Ben —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment before Laura and Rishi follow up with the technical checklist: 

- Primary objective: Run latency-sensitive inference jobs for financial workloads with strict data isolation.
- Deployment modes on the table: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs), Private VPC (SkyBridge preference given compliance).
- Key security ask: No uncontrolled public egress for inference traffic; security team wants egress through allowlisted IPs or an inline egress proxy.
- Questions we flagged to clarify:
  1) Does SkyBridge require outbound traffic to Redwood to originate from a fixed set of customer-visible IPs (allowlist), or is transit through a managed egress gateway acceptable?
  2) PrivateLink vs VPC Peering preference for your network team — any constraints (peering across accounts, transitive routing)?
  3) Is tenant-level routing required (per-customer VPC isolation) or will a shared managed VPC with strict IAM + encryption suffice?

Action items (next):
- Laura: propose a short network preflight checklist and minimal AWS/GCP config snippets.
- Rishi: call out Dedicated capacity implications if you need guaranteed single-tenant GPUs.
- Maya/Ben: share any firewall/IP ranges, SSO/KMS requirements, and a copy of the relevant security checklist if possible.

I attached the initial SOW draft we mentioned and a rough network diagram. I’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up with your security and infra owners — propose Wed next week.

Thanks,

On Thu, Dec 1, 2027 at 10:15 AM Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment before Laura and Rishi follow up with the technical checklist: 

Thanks Connor — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Security posture: Our compliance team requires that inference traffic to external model endpoints does not egress directly from our subnets to the public internet. All outbound calls must traverse a company-controlled egress point (either a NAT with static IPs that we own or an egress proxy inside our VPC).
- IP allowlist: We can maintain an allowlist on our side but need Redwood to provide stable egress IPs (or support PrivateLink so traffic stays inside the cloud provider fabric).
- PrivateLink vs Peering: Prefer PrivateLink for production due to simpler ownership boundaries (no cross-account routing). Peering may be acceptable for a POC if there are no transitive routing requirements.
- Tenant isolation: Ideally each tenant (business unit) maps to a separate VPC/namespace on our side. For Redwood, per-customer logical isolation is sufficient as long as there are separate encryption keys and audit logs.

I attached the short security intake our team uses (high level). We can share the full checklist in advance of the next meeting.

Maya Sharma
Head of Infrastructure | SkyBridge AI
maya@skybridge.ai

Subject: RE: Private VPC: Tenant isolation & egress model clarification

Hi Maya —

Thanks for the details. Based on what you shared, here are two viable patterns and the minimal network requirements for each. I’m attaching a one-page preflight checklist (redwood_private_vpc_checklist.xlsx) you can pass to NetOps.

1) PrivateLink (recommended for production)
   - Behavior: Traffic from your VPC -> AWS PrivateLink endpoint -> Redwood-managed service endpoint (stays within AWS backbone).
   - Egress: No public egress required. If Redwood initiates callbacks to your environment (webhooks, metrics) we can source those from a small set of managed outbound IPs; documented static IPs will be provided in staging/production.
   - Requirements from SkyBridge: Create a VPC Endpoint Service acceptance rule or accept the endpoint connections; provide allowlist for the subnets where endpoints will be created.
   - IAM/KMS: Customer-managed keys supported for data at rest in Private deployments; we can integrate with your KMS via cross-account access.

2) VPC Peering (acceptable for POC)
   - Behavior: Simple L3 peering; you own route tables and egress.
   - Egress: If peering, you must ensure no public internet route on the peered subnets for inference traffic — this is on your side.

Minimal technical checklist (high level):
- CIDR ranges: please confirm the IP ranges for the subnets that will host endpoints (e.g., 10.23.0.0/24).
- Required ports: 443 outbound to Redwood endpoint(s); if using PrivateLink we only need TLS to the endpoint.
- Route tables: route for the PrivateLink endpoints or peering connection.
- Security groups: allow outbound to Redwood endpoints; Redwood will provide SG IDs for inbound rules if we create endpoints in your account.
- DNS: ensure private zone resolution can resolve the Redwood endpoint hostnames when using PrivateLink.

Notes on Dedicated capacity: if you require dedicated GPU pools resident in your VPC (on-prem or colocated), that becomes a Private deployment with additional steps (hardware placement, HSM if required). Rishi, I’ll let you expand.

Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Quick note from infra:
- If SkyBridge expects no public egress, PrivateLink is our path of least resistance and gives us the cleanest network model.
- For allowlisted egress IPs (for callbacks/metric pushes), we can publish a stable pool but SLA for immutability depends on capacity changes. We recommend using PrivateLink + a small set of managed egress IPs for third-party callbacks.
- Dedicated capacity (single-tenant GPUs) is feasible but will require a short procurement lead and a mapped rollout plan; that affects pricing.

I’ll prepare a short ops runbook describing the peering/endpoint acceptance flow and the firewall rules we need.

—Rishi
